errors.english: This occurs for the meaning understood as the object
errors.why: དོན་དུ་རྟོགས་པ is the meaning understood by implication (arthāt), as opposed to the literal word; 'understood as the object' loses the point of the objection.

errors.english: Not making it a particular in that way is for the sake of making it a particular because it does not prove it as it is.
errors.why: The Tibetan says: because without such a qualification it does not prove [the thesis] as it is, it must be qualified; rendering ཁྱད་པར་དུ་བྱ ('qualify') as 'make a particular' turns the sentence into a self-contradiction.

note: Follows the Tibetan closely but renders ཁྱད་པར་དུ་བྱ ('qualify, specify') as 'make a particular' throughout, which obscures a dense argument about qualifying the statement of similarity.

errors.english: "residing completely" refers to the holy life
errors.why: ཡོངས་སུ་གནས་པ here is the Vinaya technical term pārivāsika, a monk under probation (as the next side, where he expels a monk, confirms), not 'residing completely'.

errors.english: In a ritual of motion with four actions
errors.why: This is the jñapticaturtha karman, an act with the motion as fourth (motion plus three proclamations), not a motion with four actions; likewise གསོལ་བ་དང་གཉིས་ is motion plus one proclamation.

note: A sound rendering of the karmavācanā completion rule and the Upāli boundary passage; the Vinaya procedural terms are rendered loosely.

errors.english: gather extraordinary, non-common faults of the wise
errors.why: མཁས་པ here qualifies the misdeeds as 'apt at bringing no small harm', unshared by others; they are not 'faults of the wise'.

note: A faithful and readable translation of the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son illustrations and the verse on pride; one misparsed compound in the opening sentence.
Both the Sanskrit and the Tibetan verses of the bilingual Avadānakalpalatā side are accurately and elegantly rendered.

errors.english: this (Pramāṇavārttika) Commentary on Valid Cognition, Dharmakīrti's chief work on logic set out
errors.why: The Tibetan has only 'this Vārttika'; the unmarked glosses here and on ཤ་པ ('a kind of tree, the stock example of a reason based on identity') are run into the sentence and make it hard to parse.

note: The argument on the reason's indeterminate capacity to make known and the objection about conjunction is rendered accurately; unmarked explanatory glosses clutter one passage.

errors.english: away from what is not harmful
errors.why: The Tibetan says one should turn both oneself and others away from what is harmful.

fix.find: away from what is not harmful

errors.english: the remainderless state [note: referring to nirvana with remainder]
errors.why: ལྷག་མ་ལུས་པ means 'with remainder' (sopadhiśeṣa nirvāṇa), the first of the two nirvāṇas; 'remainderless' says the opposite and contradicts the note.

fix.find: the remainderless state [note: referring to nirvana with remainder]

errors.why: ཀླུ་འཇོག་པོ is the nāga king Takṣaka; the name is left as an untranslated Tibetan word.

note: The introduction on purpose and connection reads well, but it reverses the closing instruction about harm and mislabels the nirvāṇa with remainder.

errors.english: to refute the position that harms the [note: proper view of the] self
errors.why: The consequence that follows is an objection against the selflessness thesis (if there are no beings, for whom compassion?), so the phrase means refuting what harms our [position]; the note points the reader the wrong way.

note: An accurate rendering of the three-times analysis of mind and the plantain-tree example; one misleading note at the transition.

errors.why: ཞི་བ (and ཞི་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས above) is most likely a personal name (Śānta/Śāntā) in the story of the curd pot thrown at someone's head, not 'tranquil'.
མཉམ་པ་ཉིད is sameness or equality of mind between the parties, not equanimity (བཏང་སྙོམས).

note: Lexical glosses on the Vinayavastu are mostly rendered correctly; a probable proper name is translated as an adjective.

errors.why: བདག་ཉིད here is simply the reflexive 'oneself' glossing svayam, not a soul.

errors.english: since things like a rabbit's horns are seen to be non-existent, this line of reasoning
errors.why: The point is that this reason (being unproduced) is seen to occur in non-existents such as a hare's horn, and so it proves the subject, space, to be non-existent; the English loses the reason's occurrence in the non-existent.

errors.english: during a debate the treatise itself is not the primary thing being accepted
errors.why: The Tibetan says flatly that during debate a treatise is not to be accepted at all, and that even if it has been accepted only what one oneself intends is the probandum.

note: The overall argument on svayam in the thesis definition comes through, but the key gloss is mistranslated and two steps of the argument are blurred.

errors.english: the Tathagatas [note: the Buddhas], who bring supreme light, performed
errors.why: It is the Buddha himself (Skt. tathāgataḥ, singular) who honoured his father Śuddhodana's body and built the stūpa; དག is honorific and does not mean several Buddhas.

fix.find: the Tathagatas [note: the Buddhas], who bring supreme light, performed
fix.replace: the Tathagata [note: the Buddha], who brings supreme light, performed

note: A good rendering of the Tibetan verses (the Sanskrit is only transliterated); the one real slip turns the Buddha's honouring of his father into an act of several Buddhas.
